published_prior_art.cite: DongHeiler2026 identifies selected-complier outcome mixtures under the same conditional weak-selection model, but not an ordinal same-unit coupling capacity.
DongHeiler2026 gives sharp survivor-complier mean bounds; LuDingDasgupta2018 gives fixed-marginal ordinal-benefit bounds; neither states the directional partial-subcoupling benefit interval.

repo_prior_art.cite: pid_benefit_concordance_band: a different failed dependence-restriction proposal, not a survivor-complier IV completion theorem.

published_prior_art.cite: LuDingDasgupta2018 constructs fixed-marginal extremal matrices, but does not lift an unequal survivor-complier subcoupling through IV, compliance, and selection strata.
GabrielSachsJensen2024 provides finite ordinal-benefit computations under noncompliance, but not the proposed general ordered partial-transport flow reduction.
A worked numerical witness is useful validation but is not an independent result beyond the threshold theorem.
LuDingDasgupta2018 Proposition 2, equation (6), already gives the strict-benefit fixed-marginal bound; the proposed result is a necessary nesting reduction.
FangSantos2019 supplies the directional delta/resampling substrate; the composed finite-cell endpoint map is specialized but plausibly new.
FangSantos2019, ChernozhukovLeeRosen2013, and Semenova2025 treat constituent nonsmooth or localized-inference problems, not their stated joint two-endpoint moving-support problem.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1 (sharp threshold interval)
novelty_flags.one_line: The flagship aspirant names four comparator bibkeys but gives no page, theorem, equation, or quoted open-problem anchor for the asserted partial-transport gap.

novelty_flags.label: Project-level related-work survey
novelty_flags.one_line: Add and distinguish de Aguas, Krumscheid, Pensar, and Biele (2024/2025) on tiered/stratum-specific probability-of-benefit bounds and nonregular inference; it is a closer estimand-and-inference comparator than the generic directional-bootstrap citations.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 4 (no-selection reduction)
soundness_flags.one_line: This submodel explicitly drops direction-margin and imposes q0(x)=q1(x), but σ(x)=sgn{q1(x)-q0(x)} is then outside its declared {-1,+1} range, so Γ_x^σ and the displayed reduction are undefined.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper uses conditional IV assumptions and weak sample-selection monotonicity specifically for compliers, permits selection direction to vary with X, and explicitly assigns zero selection-effect cells to the positive-direction class for identification.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics 43(5), 2018
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives sharp lower and upper bounds for the strict-benefit probability under fixed ordinal potential-outcome marginals, with constructive attaining matrices described immediately afterward.
The paper studies probability of benefit under observational and noncompliance DAGs, gives ordinal noncompliance results separately for K=3 through 7, and uses m-out-of-n bootstrap inference.

source_verification_receipts.version: author preprint corresponding to the later Journal of Econometrics article
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 8–9, Assumption 2 and equations (4.1)–(4.2); pp. 19–20, Assumption 5
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The accessible version defines covariate-conditional selection monotonicity and separately treats fuzzy Lee bounds; the published bibliographic record is Journal of Econometrics 251, 106055, not volume 249.
The paper derives survivor-complier mean-effect bounds through bounds on a survivor-complier proportion and survivor intention-to-treat effect, rather than a same-unit ordinal benefit coupling.

source_verification_receipts.version: UAI 2024 Causal Inference Workshop proceedings contribution
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: This work studies stratum-specific probability-of-benefit bounds with thresholds and nonregular inference, making it a close omitted comparator despite its different continuous-outcome, no-selection setting.

Add exact anchors for the flagship theorem: Dong–Heiler Assumption 3.2 and its selected-mixture formulas, Lu–Ding–Dasgupta Proposition 2/equation (6), and the exact Gabriel result being surpassed; explicitly compare against de Aguas et al.'s tiered-benefit inference.

Separate identification from inference at zero selection-effect cells: retain a tie-safe identification theorem, then formulate the fixed direction-margin condition solely as an inference regime and investigate whether the face-aware procedure can cover shrinking direction gaps.
